chapters.title: Why it really ended (your side of it)
chapters.teaser: Not who was right. What your soul was doing while it fell apart.

chapters.title: Your breakup pattern
chapters.teaser: How you end things, how you grieve, and the habit that slows you down.

chapters.title: Why you keep checking
chapters.teaser: What the pull back toward them is really asking for.

chapters.title: So, will they come back? The honest answer
chapters.teaser: What a chart can and can't tell you, and the question that matters more.

chapters.title: If they ever reach out
chapters.teaser: Three questions to ask before you reply, built for your soul.

chapters.title: What you do now
chapters.teaser: The next small steps that help, whatever they decide.

text.why-it-ended: Byeong Fire is the sun. You shine on everyone, generously and loudly, and that's your magic. In a relationship, though, the sun can be a lot. You may have filled every room, every plan, every silence, and your partner might have loved your energy while still feeling slightly invisible next to it. Or it went the other way: you gave warmth and got a cooler climate back, until you burned out and stopped trying. Sun types often end things with a big honest explosion or a sudden total loss of interest. Either way, it rarely came from nowhere. Look at the months before. The clues were in the weather.
text.your-breakup-pattern: You grieve out loud. Byeong Fire tells friends, posts the sad song, cries in the car, then goes out dancing three days later. People think you've moved on fast. Sometimes you have. Sometimes you've just moved the feelings somewhere less visible. Your pattern is replacing the warmth quickly, with a new crush or a packed social calendar, because a sun hates a cloudy sky. Fun is good medicine. But the lesson tends to slip away if you outrun it. Give yourself one boring, quiet weekend. The sad part doesn't last forever, and you're braver standing still than you are when you're busy.
text.the-pull: What pulls you back is the memory of the best days, the big ones. The trip, the night you laughed until four, the way they looked at you when you walked in. Byeong Fire remembers in full colour and forgets in grey. Your brain is showing you the highlight reel and cutting the footage of feeling ignored or bored. It helps to write the full version: three great memories and three times you felt dim around them. Read both lists side by side. Missing someone is valid. So is noticing that you miss the light more than the person standing in it.
text.the-honest-answer: Nobody can see another person's choices in your chart, so we won't pretend to. What we can see is how you love. You love openly, and when you're hurt you can switch from full sun to total eclipse. If you're wondering about them coming back, ask what you'd need to stay warm without burning out. Would they meet your energy? Would you leave room for theirs? A reunion that just reheats the old dynamic won't hold. What's actually in your hands is how you shine next time: generously, but not on people who keep their curtains shut.
text.if-they-reach-out: If they text, you'll want to answer instantly with a paragraph and three emojis. That's your charm. Hold it for one evening. Byeong Fire decides in the moment and regrets at leisure. Ask yourself: is this about me, or about them feeling lonely on a Tuesday? Are they offering anything new, or just checking that the sun still rises? If you do meet, meet in daylight, literally, somewhere public and short. Listen more than you perform. If it feels like the same old weather, a warm take care is enough. You can be kind without being available.
text.what-you-do-now: Shine on yourself first. Byeong Fire spends most of its light on other people, so turn some of it inward for a while. Take yourself on the dates you'd plan for someone else. Get sunlight, movement, music loud in the kitchen. See your friends, and tell one of them the unpolished version of how you feel. Then put your energy into something that's only yours: a creative project, a skill, a trip you've wanted for ages. The goal isn't to look okay. It's to feel okay when nobody's watching. That version of you chooses far better next time.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your warmth was real, Byeong. They felt it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They also felt there was no room left in the spotlight.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: It's okay to grieve loudly. That's honest.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Grieving loudly, fine. A new crush in four days? Slow down.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Write down the dim days too, not just the highlights.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You miss the glow. The glow was always yours. Keep it.

spring.intro: A spring sun rises into a world that's growing just for it. Wood ruled your birth season and Wood feeds Fire, so you were born well fuelled, Byeong: optimistic, generous, sure that warmth fixes things. In the relationship you probably believed love would win if you just shone harder. When it ended, the shock was less about them and more about a rule breaking. You gave light and it wasn't enough. That's hard for a spring sun to accept. The pull back often comes from there rather than from missing the person. You want to prove the rule still works. It does. Just not on everyone, and never as a way to earn someone staying.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Shining harder was never going to fix it. Some people just prefer shade.

summer.intro: Born in summer, you're the sun at noon, Byeong. Fire ruled the season and doubled your own element, so your chart runs hot: big feelings, big presence, big exits. Breakups for summer suns tend to be dramatic and then strangely fast. Either you blazed through the hurt in a week of loud nights out, or you burned so bright in the fights that there was nothing left to say. The blind spot is heat. Too much of it and nothing near you can grow, including a relationship. If you keep checking their stories, notice whether you're looking for them or for proof they still feel your warmth. Let noon cool to afternoon. That's where you see clearly.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Three nights out in a row is not closure. It's a heatwave.

autumn.intro: An autumn sun sits lower and more golden, Byeong, and it works harder for every degree of warmth. Metal ruled your birth season, and Fire's job is to melt and shape Metal. That gives your chart a practical streak: you show love through effort, plans, fixing things. In the relationship you may have treated it like a project you could forge into shape. When it broke, you probably asked what you did wrong, as if the right technique would have saved it. Some things don't melt. That's not a skill failure. The autumn sun's real strength is honesty: low light shows every detail. Use it on the relationship as it was, not the version you were building.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You worked so hard on it. That effort says lovely things about you.

winter.intro: A winter sun is precious because it's rare. Water ruled your birth season, Byeong, and Water is the element that puts out Fire. You grew up shining against the cold, which made you brave and a little defensive about your warmth. In love you may have expected the chill to arrive eventually, and braced for it. After the breakup you likely went bright on the outside and freezing underneath. Lots of laughing, little sleeping. Here's the winter truth: you're not too much. You were born into a season that tested your light, and you kept it anyway. The pull back is the worry that nobody else will feel that warm. Plenty of people already do.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You kept your light through a whole winter. That doesn't go out now.

strength.strong: Your chart feeds your fire generously, Byeong, so you blaze. In love you bring warmth, plans and a lot of presence, and when things went wrong you probably turned the heat up instead of down. More energy, more effort, more talking. The blind spot of a strong sun is that it can scorch the very thing it wants to grow. Your ex may have needed shade, and you offered spotlight. If you're thinking of reaching back, ask whether you'd be offering warmth or a performance. Dimming a little is how others get to glow near you.
strength.weak: With little to feed your flame, Byeong, you learned to shine on borrowed fuel: approval, attention, someone's laugh. In the relationship you may have given warmth constantly and quietly run low. You smiled through things you should have named. After it ended, you might feel that nobody will love you unless you're sunny all the time. That's the shrinking talking. Your warmth is real even on cloudy days. Let people see you tired, grumpy, unsure. The ones worth keeping will stay. Refuel with rest before you shine for anyone again.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and answers, even in heartbreak. You want a plan for getting over it, maybe even a plan for getting them back. Slow down. Not everything grows on schedule, and some things need to just sit for a while. Ask for help instead of turning healing into a project. For balance, let a little Metal in: declutter, finish old things, clear out the drafts folder. A clean edge helps Wood stop reaching for what's already gone.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means fresh starts feel heavy. After a breakup you might stay in the same place, emotionally and literally, for longer than you'd like. That isn't weakness. It just means new growth needs a nudge. Small steps work best: a new route to work, one new class, one new person a week. Get outside in the mornings and keep something green near you. You don't need a whole new life. You need one new branch, and then another.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes you feel everything at full volume. A breakup can feel like an emergency, with urges to text, post, or fix it all tonight. Your passion is real, but heat isn't a strategy. Before any big move, sleep on it. Cool down with water: swimming, long showers, quiet evenings at home. Talk to your calmest friend before your most exciting one. Let the fire warm you instead of burning through your peace.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means joy and visibility don't come easily, and after a breakup you might go dim for a while, hiding from people and from fun. Turn the lights back on gently. Sunshine, music, dancing in the kitchen, one social plan a week even when you'd rather stay in. Letting people see you is the medicine here. Warmth doesn't only live in romance. It's in friends, in laughter, in simply being out in the world.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you hold on: to routines, to memories, to the hope that things will settle back into their old place. Stability is your gift, but in heartbreak it can turn into staying stuck. Shake the ground a little. Move the furniture, take a short trip, try something unplanned. Let some Wood energy in, growth and new beginnings. You can keep what was good and still leave room for something new to grow.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means life can feel unsteady, and a breakup can knock away what little ground you had. You might feel scattered, unsure where to put your feet. Build structure gently: regular meals, a steady bedtime, one place at home that's only yours. Cook something. Walk somewhere. Lean on the people who are reliable. Stability first, big decisions later. You need solid ground under you before deciding anything about the past.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal makes you sharp and decisive, sometimes too quickly. You may have cut the relationship off cleanly and then refused to look at what you feel. Or you judge yourself harshly for every mistake you made in it. Soften the edges. Let Water in: rest, tears, music, journaling. Feeling the grief isn't the same as reopening the door. You can keep your boundaries firm and still let your heart thaw.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard, so after a breakup you might keep the door half open, answer every message, or stay friends when it hurts. Practise clean edges. Mute without guilt. Box up their things. Say no without explaining. White and silver, tidy spaces and finished tasks all help your chart. A boundary isn't cold. It's how you protect the part of you that's still healing.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means you think and feel deeply, maybe endlessly. After a breakup you might drift through memories, analyse every detail, and lose sleep to what-ifs. Your intuition is a gift, but it needs riverbanks. Add some Earth: routines, cooking, walks, people who ground you. Give overthinking a time limit. Feel it fully, then get up and do one ordinary thing.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means rest and reflection get skipped. You may rush past the breakup, staying busy so you never have to sit with it. That works until suddenly it doesn't. Build in quiet on purpose: slow mornings, water by your bed, a few lines in a journal at night, a bath instead of another plan. Let yourself feel without fixing. Intuition grows when you give it some silence.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: So much Wood. You've drafted three versions of 'hey, random but' already.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy wants a goal. Give it your own plans, not their inbox.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: every feeling is a five-alarm emergency. It's a breakup, not an inferno.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is beautiful. Let it cool before you hit send on anything.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth. You'd still be in that relationship purely out of habit.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Just make sure you're loyal to yourself too.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. You cut them off cleanly, then reread everything at midnight.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Being firm protected you. Being gentle with yourself will heal you.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've cried to three songs and written a novel in your notes app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Feeling deeply is a gift. Just come up for air sometimes.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make moving on feel stuck. Small new routines count as growth.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: You haven't changed anything since the breakup, including your lock screen. Start there.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make joy feel far away. Borrow some from a loud friend.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: You stopped having fun when they left. Fun was never theirs to take.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth can make everything feel unsteady. Simple routines will hold you.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no anchor. You re-decide whether to text them every hour.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal makes boundaries tricky. You're allowed to say no to your own phone.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means you'll answer at 2am. Put the phone in another room.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make grief hide. It's okay to let it surface slowly.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: You said you're fine twelve times today. Water would like a word.

gap-wood.title: Firewood for the sun
gap-wood.text: You dated a tree, and trees don't announce they're tired. That's the confusing part. Your Gap Wood ex seemed endlessly solid: they drove, they planned, they listened to your stories at 1am and asked smart questions. You flooded their phone with dog photos and capital letters, vanished for a day because life got loud, then came back glowing. They never complained. And then, from your side, out of a clear sky, they were finished. No big fight. Just a calm, final conversation that you have probably replayed forty times. Here's the honest bit, said kindly: they were keeping a tally you couldn't see, and the gaps in your texting were on it. It wasn't that you were selfish. You shine outward and assumed the light was reaching them. What you miss is how held they made you feel, like solid ground under a stage. Missing that is fair. The practice for you is noticing the quiet ones. Ask the friend who never asks for anything how they're actually doing, and wait through the pause. That small skill changes how your warmth lands, with everyone.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, you gave so much light. You just forgot to check who was holding the match.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap, you counted every unanswered text and said nothing. That's not patience, that's a ledger.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Both of you were generous. Neither of you said 'I'm tired.' Start there.

eul-wood.title: The flower that faded in full sun
eul-wood.text: You loved a flower and gave it all the sun you had, which is a lot. Your Eul Wood ex bloomed around you: laughing at your stories, coming to every party, fitting into your noisy life like they'd always been there. You called instead of texting, sent hearts by the dozen, made big plans and occasionally forgot the small ones. They remembered everything. And slowly they started fading at the edges of your brightness, and when they tried to get your attention in quieter ways, a cool reply, a sudden distance, you thought they were playing games. You got frustrated. They felt unseen. Neither of you was wrong about what you felt. Your sting is confusion: you were so warm, how was it not enough? It was warm. It just wasn't aimed. What you miss is how they made your light feel welcome, never too much. The next skill is focus. Pick one friend this week and give them a whole evening where you ask the questions and keep your own stories short. It's not dimming yourself. It's pointing the light.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, a hundred heart emojis can't fix forgetting their plans twice.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, you were allowed to just say 'I need you to notice me.'

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Too much sun scorches. Hints in the shade get missed. Both fixable.

byeong-fire.title: Two suns, one spotlight
byeong-fire.text: Dating another Byeong Fire was like living inside a festival. Caps lock texts, voice notes from the street, video calls from a karaoke booth. You understood each other's energy instantly: nobody had to apologise for being loud. But there was one spotlight and two people who need to stand in it. Stories became contests. Birthdays became who-planned-it-better. You were both generous, both warm, and both much better at talking than listening. And here's the real problem: suns burn bright and then crash, and when you crashed at the same time, there was nobody left to tend the fire. Two exhausted people on a sofa, each waiting to be cheered up, each too proud to go first. It wasn't a lack of love. It was a lack of shade. The fun is what pulls you back. Life with them was never boring, and normal life feels slow and grey by comparison. What you can do is become a better listener on purpose. Ask a friend a real question and say nothing about yourself for the whole conversation. It's hard. It's also exactly what a sun needs to learn, with any partner.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Two suns. One sky. Who did the dishes? Nobody. Nobody did the dishes.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You both gave so much warmth. You just needed someone to sit in it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Listen for one whole conversation. Then tell me it's not a superpower.

jeong-fire.title: The sun and the candle in different rooms
jeong-fire.text: You spread warmth across the whole sky, and your Jeong Fire ex wanted it in one room, on them. You sent lots of short, loud messages to lots of people; they sent fewer, deeper ones and noticed exactly whose message you answered first. When you posted from a party, they saw it before you'd sent them a word. To you, friends are part of the fun. To them, being one of many felt like not being the one. They called it hurt; you called it heavy. When arguments flared, they flared fast, both of you hot, and you forgot by morning while they kept the whole transcript. So you thought you'd made up. They thought you'd just moved on. Their intensity is what you miss. Nobody else ever looked at you like you were the only light in the world. Practise the first reply. When someone you love messages, answer them before the group chat. It's small, and it says 'you come first' without making a speech about it. A sun can choose where it shines first.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, you wanted to be first. That's a fair thing to want.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, replying to the group chat before your partner is a statement.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Same fire, different rooms. Next time, open the door between them.

mu-earth.title: Sunlight on a mountain that stayed home
mu-earth.text: Your Mu Earth ex was the mountain you warmed every morning, and for a while that was beautiful. You brought the plans, the celebrations, the spontaneous road trip. They brought steadiness, a home base, and one sincere text for every twelve of yours. You wanted to move, change, go out; they wanted to stay in, thank you. At first that balanced you. Then you started finding them slow, and they started finding you exhausting. In arguments you flared and they went silent, and their silence made you louder, which made them more silent. That's how this one wore down: no betrayal, just the sun shouting at a mountain that had already decided not to move. What you keep reaching for is the solidity. When your own energy crashed, they were still there, still the same, and you've noticed how much you leaned on that. Judge love by quality, not quantity. Look at their one sincere sentence and your twelve exclamation marks, and ask which carried more weight. Then practise saying fewer, truer things to people you care about.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, a quick 'haha' costs nothing. Use it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, their one sentence meant more than your twelve. Count better.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sun and mountain. Gorgeous view. Terrible at arguments.

gi-earth.title: Sun on the garden, nobody watering
gi-earth.text: Things grew when you two were together, and you can probably still feel that. Your Gi Earth ex made your big, bright life work: they remembered the dentist appointment, the friend's birthday, the electricity bill you were definitely going to pay. You brought sunshine; they brought soil. The cracks came from the small stuff. You forgot errands, and they noticed every one. They worried, and you called it negativity and tried to cheer them up. They answered your messages with practical questions; you answered theirs with three emojis and half a sentence. Slowly they became the responsible one, cleaning up after the sun, and you started to feel nagged. You weren't careless on purpose, and it still dried them out. Being looked after is what you miss. They made you feel safe enough to shine. Answer the question you were asked. When someone checks in about a practical thing, deal with it first and joke second. It's an unglamorous skill, and it would have changed everything in that garden.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, you're allowed to stop managing and just enjoy the sun.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, forgetting the errand once is cute. Forty times is a pattern.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Things grew here. That part was real.

gyeong-metal.title: The sun and the blade, forging sparks
gyeong-metal.text: You wanted celebration; your Gyeong Metal ex wanted results. You sent emojis and excitement; they sent 'ok.' with a full stop, and you took it personally every single time. They meant it neutrally. You couldn't hear it that way. Your heat put pressure on them, the way fire does on metal, and they resisted being softened. Their bluntness dimmed your mood in seconds, and your overbearing energy made them dig in. Fights were loud and quick and nobody really won. There's a reason this pairing is called forging: it can make something strong, but it's hot, hard work, and you both got tired of the sparks. Feeling like your warmth was treated as noise is the part that lingers. Their respect is what you crave again. When they were proud of you, it meant something, because they don't hand out praise. Try not to measure love in enthusiasm. Some people show care by being reliable and plain. Practise reading short as short, not cold. It will save you a lot of 2am overthinking, with anyone.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gyeong, 'ok.' with a full stop after their good news? Brutal.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, short isn't cold. Some people just don't decorate.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Forging takes heat and patience. You had the heat.

sin-metal.title: Sunlight on a jewel
sin-metal.text: This was one of the great pairings, a Heavenly Combination, sunlight hitting a jewel. You made your Sin Metal ex sparkle, and they made your warmth look elegant. People noticed you as a couple. The trouble was always in the details. You were careless with words sometimes, forgot the thing they mentioned, filled quiet evenings with noise. Sin is sensitive to being overlooked, and when they felt neglected they withdrew or turned sharp, and you found their standards exhausting. You'd send warm, frequent, excited messages; they replied beautifully, a little late, and you missed how much effort was in the reply. It was close to brilliant, and small things wore down the shine, which is a particular kind of maddening. What pulls you back is how good you looked to yourself next to them. You felt chosen by someone with taste. Practise noticing effort. When someone puts care into something for you, a text, a meal, a gift, name the specific detail you loved. That one habit turns a good match into a great one, whoever it's with.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, you deserved to have the effort noticed. Ask for it out loud.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, three emojis in reply to a perfect paragraph. Think about that.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Heavenly Combination. Still needs small, daily care.

im-water.title: The sun over the ocean
im-water.text: You were the sun and your Im Water ex was the ocean, and the view was magnificent. Big personalities, big conversations, big nights out. But water controls fire, and you felt it. Their coolness dampened your enthusiasm. When they withdrew to think, which oceans do, you took it as rejection and pushed harder, and the harder you pushed, the further out the tide went. You texted constantly; they texted in bursts or not at all. You felt ignored; they felt flooded. And on their low days, their mood could put out your joy entirely, which made you wonder where your light had gone. You lost a little of yourself trying to be warm enough for someone who mostly needed space. Their depth is what you miss. They saw through your performance to something real, and that felt like being known. Practise letting silence be silence. Next time someone doesn't reply for a few hours, do something you love instead of checking your phone. A sun doesn't need permission to shine, or a read receipt.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, a photo of your coffee once a day. That's it. That's the fix.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, their silence wasn't rejection. Oceans need room.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Magnificent view, wrong thermostat.

gye-water.title: Sunshine and drizzle
gye-water.text: Rainbow weather, people called it, and that's what it was: gorgeous when the light and the rain met, confusing the rest of the time. Your Gye Water ex was quiet and deep. You were loud and bright. You sent messages, emojis, voice notes; they replied slowly and thoughtfully, or not at all, and you read their quiet as disinterest. Your bluntness, which you think of as honesty, landed on them as insensitivity. And your habit of joking through tension, which works with most people, made them feel unheard. They withdrew; you pushed; the sky turned stormy. You couldn't make them happy, and you are someone used to making people happy. That's the bit that bruises. The mystery is what pulls you. They were the one person you couldn't quite figure out. When someone you love is low, don't fix it with a joke. Sit there. Say 'I'm here.' Let the quiet be the conversation. It feels unbearable for about a minute. Then it feels like closeness.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, 'still here, just quiet' is a whole love letter to a sun.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Byeong, joking through their sadness isn't comforting. It's dodging.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Rainbows need both. That part was true.
